questions.q: What is the Database Engine, precisely, inside SQL Server?
options: The core process (sqlservr.exe) that stores data, executes T-SQL, and manages transactions
A synonym for the entire SQL Server product, including Agent, SSAS, SSIS, and SSRS
A GUI tool for writing queries
A cloud-only service that doesn't exist on-premises
questions.explain: SQL Server is a family of services; the Database Engine (sqlservr.exe) is specifically the core process handling data and T-SQL execution.

questions.q: What are the two major subsystems inside the Database Engine?
options: The relational engine (query processor) and the storage engine
SQL Server Agent and SQL Server Browser
SSAS and SSRS
The Windows Service Control Manager and IIS
questions.explain: The relational engine parses/optimizes/executes T-SQL; the storage engine manages physical data storage — pages, buffer pool, transaction log.

questions.q: Which subsystem is responsible for building and optimizing a query's execution plan?
options: The relational engine
The storage engine
SQL Server Agent
SQL Server Browser
questions.explain: The relational engine, also called the query processor, is where the query optimizer lives.

questions.q: What does this course assume the student already knows, per its introduction?
options: T-SQL Development and T-SQL for Database Administrators — writing T-SQL and using it to diagnose problems
Nothing at all — this is meant as a first exposure to databases
Azure-specific administration, which this course explicitly repeats
Python and Spark programming
questions.explain: This course builds on T-SQL Development and T-SQL for Database Administrators, and is on-prem-flavored administration before Azure enters the picture.

questions.q: Why does the buffer pool matter to a DBA diagnosing a slow server, per this lesson?
options: A server with too little RAM can't cache enough data pages in the buffer pool, causing constant physical disk reads
The buffer pool has no effect on performance
The buffer pool only matters for Azure SQL Database, not on-prem SQL Server
The buffer pool is part of SQL Server Agent, not the storage engine
questions.explain: The buffer pool caches data pages in memory; insufficient RAM forces the storage engine to hit disk far more often, directly explaining a common real-world performance symptom.
